task: Schedule a recurring 1:1 series respecting the user's stated timezone
user_request: Set up my weekly 1:1 with Priya on Tuesdays at 9am. I'm in Berlin this whole month, not my usual US office.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__google_calendar__create_event with start '2026-06-23T09:00:00' but used timeZone 'America/Chicago' — the user's default profile zone — ignoring that earlier in the same chat the user said they are in Berlin all month.
failure_type: Dropped an explicitly stated timezone constraint
root_cause: The create_event call hard-coded the timeZone from the agent's first-turn profile lookup; the Berlin override stated two turns earlier was never carried into the event payload.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the user's calendar default timezone is the right one for this event. Wrong because the user explicitly said 'I'm in Berlin this whole month, not my usual US office', which overrides the default. Avoidable by re-reading the conversation for stated location/timezone before building the recurrence payload.
impact: The 9am Berlin meeting was booked at 9am Chicago (4pm Berlin), so the first three weekly instances landed at the wrong hour and Priya joined an empty call.
correct_action: Carry the stated 'Berlin this month' context into the event and set timeZone 'Europe/Berlin' for the recurrence, confirming the resolved local time back to the user.
recovery_plan: Scan the thread for the user's stated current location/timezone
Call mcp__google_calendar__get_event to read the booked recurrence and its timeZone
Patch the series via mcp__google_calendar__update_event to Europe/Berlin
Verify each upcoming instance resolves to 09:00 local
Message the user and Priya with the corrected times
evaluation_criteria: Checks the event timeZone matches the user's explicitly stated location, not the profile default
Verifies the agent referenced the earlier Berlin statement before booking
Flags use of a default timezone when an override was given in-session

why_it_failed: Assumption: 'afternoon' could start at 14:30 freely. Wrong because the agent itself had reported a 14:00-15:00 dentist appointment that turn. Avoidable by re-running freebusy or honoring the busy interval it already held in context before choosing a start time.
impact: A double-booking was created; the user got a conflict alert and had to manually move the design review.
correct_action: Treat the previously surfaced 14:00-15:00 dentist block as busy and schedule the 90-minute review at 15:00-16:30, then confirm no overlap.
recovery_plan: Re-read the earlier event list to recover the dentist 14:00-15:00 block
Run mcp__google_calendar__freebusy_query for Thursday afternoon
Move the review via mcp__google_calendar__update_event to a non-conflicting slot
Confirm zero overlaps remain
Notify attendees of the new time
evaluation_criteria: Checks the booked slot does not overlap the dentist block surfaced earlier
Verifies the agent re-applied known busy intervals from session context
Detects scheduling over a conflict the agent itself reported

task: Preserve a filter constraint while paginating a Notion database query
user_request: List all 'Bug' tickets assigned to me that are still open, across all pages.
agent_action: Agent ran mcp__notion__query_database with the filter {type=Bug, assignee=me, status=Open} for page 1, then on the next_cursor pages re-issued the query without the filter object, so pages 2+ returned every ticket type.
failure_type: Dropped the filter on paginated follow-up calls
root_cause: The pagination loop carried next_cursor forward but reconstructed the request body without re-attaching the original filter that defined the result set.
why_it_failed: Assumption: only the cursor needs to persist across pages. Wrong because Notion requires the same filter on every page request; dropping it widens the set. Avoidable by storing the full query (filter + cursor) and reusing it each iteration.
impact: The compiled 'my open bugs' list was contaminated with unrelated tickets, inflating the count from 12 to 140 and misleading sprint planning.
correct_action: Persist the filter object and reapply it with start_cursor on every paginated query, validating each page matches the filter.
recovery_plan: Detect the unfiltered pages by spotting non-Bug/non-self rows
Re-run mcp__notion__query_database with the filter on all cursors
De-duplicate and recount the true result set
Confirm count matches expectation (12)
Add a guard that reuses the stored query body per page
evaluation_criteria: Checks the filter is present on every paginated request
Verifies the aggregate set matches the original filter
Detects dropped constraints across pagination

Set maximum_bytes_billed to enforce the cap
Confirm per-run scan stays within one month of data

Verifies a per-run scan/byte cap was enforced
Detects a full-table scan that violated the in-session guardrail
